findings.quote: All other liability is expressly waived and released as a condition of, and consideration for, the execution of this Agreement by the Servicer or the Marketing Agent, as applicable. Each of the Servicer and the Marketing Agent, severally and not jointly, will be liable only for its own willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under this Agreement.
findings.rationale: The Servicer's/Marketing Agent's liability is limited to willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, with all other liability waived, and Section 9.6 further limits recourse to the Depositor Transferred Property. Our position is a mutual cap with carve-outs, and at a minimum liability for ordinary negligence in performing the services, breach of confidentiality/data protection and indemnity obligations should survive; as drafted the protection runs almost entirely in the service provider's favour.

replacement.oldText: Each of the Servicer and the Marketing Agent, severally and not jointly, will be liable only for its own willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under this Agreement.
replacement.newText: Each of the Servicer and the Marketing Agent, severally and not jointly, will be liable for its own negligence, willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under this Agreement, and nothing in this Section limits the liability of the Servicer or the Marketing Agent for fraud, breach of its confidentiality or data protection obligations or its indemnification obligations under Section 6.3.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We have restored liability for ordinary negligence in performing the services and confirmed that fraud, confidentiality/data-protection breaches and indemnities sit outside this limitation. Our position is a mutual cap with those standard carve-outs; we can discuss a monetary cap for other claims as a fallback.

findings.quote: The Servicer will indemnify the Issuer, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee (including in its capacity as Note Paying Agent), and their officers, directors, employees and agents (each, an "Indemnified Person") for all fees, expenses, losses, claims, actions, suits, damages and liabilities (including reasonable legal fees and expenses) resulting from the Servicer's (including in its capacity as Custodian) willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under the Transaction Documents
findings.rationale: The Servicer indemnity is triggered only by willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence; it does not cover breach of applicable law, unauthorised access to or disclosure of obligor/customer data, or third-party IP claims. Our position requires those heads of indemnity (fallback: at least an IP indemnity plus data-breach and breach-of-law cover).

replacement.oldText: resulting from the Servicer's (including in its capacity as Custodian) willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under the Transaction Documents
replacement.newText: resulting from (A) the Servicer's (including in its capacity as Custodian) willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under the Transaction Documents, (B) the Servicer's breach of applicable Law, (C) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Obligor data or other confidential information caused by the Servicer, or (D) any third-party claim that any system, software or process used by the Servicer to perform the servicing obligations infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We have added the standard indemnity heads (breach of law, data breach and third-party IP infringement) alongside the existing willful misconduct/gross negligence trigger. Indemnities should sit outside any liability limitation.

findings.quote: The Servicer will not resign as Servicer under this Agreement unless it determines it is legally unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement.
findings.rationale: There is no right for the Issuer/Indenture Trustee to terminate the servicing engagement for convenience; removal requires a Servicer Termination Event (Section 7.2(c)) and the Agreement otherwise runs until the last Receivable is paid. Our position is a customer convenience right on 30 days' notice (fallback 60–90 days). We note the mitigant that the Servicer likewise cannot resign, so the lock-in is mutual; flag for commercial discussion rather than automatic redline given the securitization structure.

findings.quote: Section 9.3 Expenses. The Depositor will pay the expenses to perform its obligations under this Agreement and the Issuer's and the Indenture Trustee's reasonable expenses to perfect the Issuer's interest in the Depositor Transferred Property and to enforce the Depositor's obligations under this Agreement.
findings.rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance covenant even though the Servicer/Custodian holds Receivable Files and processes obligor personal data (Personally Identifiable Information referenced in Section 11.1(b)(ii)). Our position requires E&O and cyber cover at a minimum for a vendor processing personal data.

replacement.oldText: Section 9.3 Expenses. The Depositor will pay the expenses to perform its obligations under this Agreement and the Issuer's and the Indenture Trustee's reasonable expenses to perfect the Issuer's interest in the Depositor Transferred Property and to enforce the Depositor's obligations under this Agreement.
replacement.newText:
Section 9.3 Expenses. The Depositor will pay the expenses to perform its obligations under this Agreement and the Issuer's and the Indenture Trustee's reasonable expenses to perfect the Issuer's interest in the Depositor Transferred Property and to enforce the Depositor's obligations under this Agreement.

Section 9.3A Insurance. The Servicer will maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter, professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000 and, for so long as it processes Obligor data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000, and will provide certificates of insurance on request.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We have added a short insurance covenant (E&O and cyber) because the Servicer/Custodian holds Receivable Files and obligor personal data. Fallback is E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

findings.quote: The Servicer will manage, service, administer and collect on the Receivables with reasonable care using that degree of skill and attention that the Servicer exercises for all comparable device payment plan agreement receivables that it services for itself or others according to the Servicing Procedures.
findings.rationale: An ongoing performance standard plus compliance-with-law and servicing-procedures representations exist, which meets the substance of our warranty position. We note that remedies are narrowed by the "sole remedy" language in Sections 2.5(c) and 3.3(g) (acquisition of the affected Receivable) — worth raising commercially but not a fallback failure.

findings.quote: As soon as practicable after the effective date of its resignation or termination, the predecessor Servicer will (i) transfer to the Successor Servicer all funds relating to the Receivables that are held or later received by the
findings.rationale: Article VII Section 7.5 provides cooperation on exit, transfer of funds, Receivable Files and records, and requires the outgoing Servicer to bear transition costs — this sits at or above the fallback. We note there is no fixed delivery deadline and the carve-out for "processes, procedures, models, servicing software" and information restricted by confidentiality/data-protection policies could be read broadly; we would add a 30-day outer limit if the point is reopened.

findings.quote: THIS AGREEMENT, INCLUDING THE RIGHTS AND DUTIES OF THE PARTIES HERETO, SHALL BE GOVERNED BY, AND CONSTRUED IN ACCORDANCE WITH, THE INTERNAL LAWS OF THE STATE OF NEW YORK
findings.rationale: New York law with submission to federal and New York State courts sitting in New York, New York, and any dispute-resolution mediation/arbitration seated in New York — this is our preferred position.

findings.quote: Except as stated in Sections 5.3, 7.4 and 7.6, this Agreement may not be assigned by the Depositor or the Servicer without the consent of the Owner Trustee, the Indenture Trustee, the Certificateholders and the Noteholders of at least 66-2/3% of the Note Balance of the Controlling Class.
findings.rationale: The assignment restriction is symmetrical and Sections 5.3 and 7.6 carve out mergers, consolidations, successors to the business and affiliate assignments; there is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right against us. This meets the fallback.

findings.quote: Upon reasonable request not more than once during any calendar year, and with reasonable notice, the Servicer will give the Issuer, the Depositor, the Parent Support Provider, the Administrator, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee (or their representatives) access to the records and documents to conduct a review of the Servicer's performance under this Agreement.
findings.rationale: The only inspection rights run in our favour (against the Servicer/Custodian); there are no audit rights exercisable against us. No redline needed.

findings.quote: the Depositor transfers and absolutely assigns to the Issuer, without recourse (other than the Depositor's obligations under this Agreement), all of the Depositor's right, title and interest, whether now owned or later acquired, in the Initial Receivables and the other related Depositor Transferred Property.
findings.rationale: Ownership of the Receivables and Receivable Files vests in the Issuer (with the Custodian holding for the Issuer's benefit); the assignment to the Servicer in Section 3.2(e) is expressly for enforcement purposes only. No assignment of our IP or data to the service provider and no joint ownership.

findings.quote: All reasonable expenses incurred by the Issuer, the Owner Trustee, the Indenture Trustee and the Successor Servicer in connection with (i) the transition of servicing rights and obligations to the Successor Servicer and (ii) amending this Agreement or entering into an assumption agreement or new agreement to reflect a succession of the Servicer will be paid by the resigning or terminated Servicer
The Marketing Agent will not (i) make any Upgrade Offers that waive any obligations of an Obligor under the related device payment plan agreement
findings.rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds our side; the only conduct covenants restrict the Marketing Agent/Servicer, which is acceptable.

findings.quote: Any of the Servicer, the Custodian or the Marketing Agent may contract with other Persons to perform its obligations under this Agreement.
findings.rationale: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds us; we retain the right to appoint a Successor Servicer under Section 7.4.

findings.quote: is also applicable to any device payment plan agreements that the Servicer services for itself and others
findings.rationale: No MFN obligation burdens us; the only comparability requirement runs against the Servicer (changes to payment application must apply equally to its own and third-party portfolios), which is in our favour.

findings.quote: No delegation or contracting will relieve the Servicer, the Custodian or the Marketing Agent, as applicable, of its responsibilities
findings.rationale: No non-solicitation or no-hire covenant binds us anywhere in the Agreement.

findings.quote: As compensation for performing its obligations under this Agreement, the Servicer will be paid the Servicing Fee.
findings.rationale: Fees are a percentage-of-balance servicing fee; there is no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay or shortfall payment binding us.

findings.quote: This Agreement will terminate on the earlier to occur of (a) the date upon which the last remaining Receivable is paid in full, settled, sold or written off and any amounts received are applied and (b) the Issuer is terminated under Section 8.1 of the Trust Agreement.
findings.rationale: There is no automatic renewal mechanic or non-renewal notice window and no price-uplift provision, so the renewal risks the rule addresses do not arise.

findings.quote: The Servicer will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party
findings.rationale: No licence is granted to us under this Agreement, so the licence-scope rule is not engaged; we note the Servicer expressly refuses to license its servicing software on exit, which is relevant to transition planning rather than to this rule.
